We remark that the sublinear convergence rate can be established for the general case [49], while in Theorem 5.12 linear convergence rate is given for a generic case. This can be interpreted via the fact that the local branches of the solution mapping for the best low rank partially orthogonal tensor approximation problem have local Lipschitz continuity whenever the nondegeneracy of the converged KKT point holds [12]. However, the nondegeneracy only holds generically. Equivalently, for general polynomial systems, only local H¨olderian error bounds can hold [34]. The explicit examples given in [16,17] present a witness for this phenomenon when r = 1.

Given that numerous problems can be recast as the NLS problem for diﬀerent choices of M and ψ, our framework is potentially applicable to the convergence analysis of numerical algorithms for them. It is possible to establish an unconditional convergence result analogous to Theorem 5.13. We also want to mention that our framework heavily relies on the geometry of M and ψ. Hence, the framework is applicable if the geometry of (M,ψ) is well-understood. Of particular interest is the case where ψ(M) is a variety of structured matrices or tensors, since such varieties are already extensively studied in the context of computational algebraic geometry [13,31,35].
